methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)

data.narrative:
Atoms is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $1.7B to date. The comparable universe in Robotics & Manufacturing spans 9 peers (1 public, 8 private), including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics, though none achieve sufficient stage/tier overlap for a robust peer-median calculation.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($1.7B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, this method implies a valuation of $2.0B. This reflects the forward-looking assumption that post-Growth financing will command a modest premium to cumulative deployment.

The Peer-Median approach is not applicable; while 11 same-sector peers exist in robotics and manufacturing, filtering for aligned stage, proximity, and valuation tier yields insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 required) to support a reliable median. Broadening to all-sector peers would introduce material bias.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B (floor, using raised capital as floor) to $2.3B (ceiling, applying 1.35x to raised capital), with a central estimate of $2.0B. Key uncertainties include the company's unit economics trajectory, capital efficiency relative to frontier-robotics benchmarks, and the timing and terms of subsequent funding rounds.
